source_admission: Published values used as constants, fitted data or cited findings; no external dataset files are admitted. 'access' records how each source was read: two literature-gathering agents fetched and quoted most of them (from scanned reports by OCR where noted), and Woodward (1976) and NACA Report 333 were read here. Secondary sources are marked. Model products of this repository are cited by path in the README and hashed in the results.

sources.citation: Woodward 1976, Interagency Workshop on Lighter Than Air Vehicles, pp. 169-176 (NTRS 19760007942, N76-15030)
sources.title: An Aerodynamic Load Criterion for Airships
sources.use: the gust bending-moment envelope: bending moment = Cm q Vol^(2/3) L, with Cm / (W0/V0) rising from 0 at the nose to 0.065 at 0.3 L and 0.10 from 0.5 to 0.65 L, then falling to 0 at the stern; the Guggenheim Airship Institute's 35 ft/s as the largest crosswind gust; the Shenandoah example (91 ft/s top speed, peak coefficient 0.0385, 3,950,000 lb ft at 0.0021 slug/ft3); the envelope covers the measured and calculated circling, rudder-reversal and rough-air moments of the Shenandoah, Los Angeles and RS-1, and only the Akron's design curve exceeds it anywhere; aerodynamic loads became as important as or preponderant over static loads by the end of the First World War
sources.access: full text (scanned), read here
